text: @guowenzhang/dsh-worktree 是 DSH Web 插件，为新会话提供独立的 Git worktree 工作区。它通过 Host worktree 服务创建分支检出，并把新会话放进该工作区；新会话界面可选择基础分支并启动隔离会话。插件还可在工具修改文件前保存副本，并在侧边栏查看变更、比较副本与当前文件或恢复文件。适合需要并行处理多个仓库任务、隔离会话文件改动并查看变更的 DSH 用户。需要 Host 环境可运行 Git。

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree is a DSH Web plugin for isolated Git worktrees. Start a new session in a branch checkout, save file copies before changes, and review, compare, or restore them in a sidebar. It suits users who want separate workspaces for parallel repository tasks. The Host needs Git.
想让每个 DSH 新会话都在独立的 Git worktree 里运行。
怎样从指定分支创建隔离工作区并开始会话？
我想查看会话改过的文件，并能比较或恢复先前版本。
@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree 的功能「新会话工作区」：在新会话界面选择基础分支后创建 Git worktree，并让会话在检出目录中启动。
@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree 的功能「文件变更备份与恢复」：工具可在修改前保存文件副本，侧边栏列出变更并提供比较和恢复操作。
@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree 的维护与更新元数据：已归档；距最后推送 7 天；提交数 36；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 22/100（置信度 low）。

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Why this plugin：Our project spans multiple repositories and needs parallel development. Git worktrees provide isolated workspaces so file changes from different tasks do not interfere with each other.

This plugin lets you tick `worktree` on the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) New Session screen to create an isolated workspace and start a session inside it. It can also set up submodules and nested repositories alongside the parent checkout.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Why this plugin：In the plugin list, display names and descriptions follow the Harness language setting in English or Chinese (English is the default fallback); English names use the package name without its npm scope, Chinese names describe the purpose, and installation still uses the unchanged real package name.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Screenshots：Select a base branch and tick `worktree` to create a workspace and open the new session. Unsent text, references, and attachments move with it without being submitted; a failed creation or navigation preserves the original draft.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Screenshots：The settings page carries three cards: **Git accounts** on top to connect GitHub / GitLab / Gitee, scan this machine's existing authorizations, and jump to the Git accounts page for projects; **Worktree settings** in the middle for whether new sessions start in a worktree, child repositories, scan depth, and storage location; and **Automatic backup** at the bottom for the protection switches and the change-history page. Valid changes save automatically and take effect immediately; no Save or Reset to default button is needed.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Protection before a change：**On by default.** The first time the AI is about to change a file that already exists, that file's current content is copied out of the workspace — so a bad edit or a deletion can still be recovered.

The **Automatic backup** card on the settings page has three switch rows: **Session file protection** (on by default), **Block delete commands** (on by default), and **Show the change history sidebar** (on by default). Changes take effect immediately, with no restart.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Protection before a change：Copies live in `~/.agents/file-guard/<session hash>/` and **mirror the workspace layout**, so recovery is copying the file back: no tool and no index needed. Files outside the working directory (another folder, another drive) go under `external/` with their own path preserved. **The copy is byte-level, so format does not matter**: `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` are treated exactly like `.txt`.

Two things trigger a copy:

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Protection before a change：- **Automatic**: only `write` and `edit` copy their target *before* the write, at about 1 ms per file. Read-only tools such as `read` and `read_image` do not create backups.
- **Declared by the model**: before changing files whose targets no argument names, the AI is asked to call the `worktree_backup` tool with those paths. It has no scope limit — paths outside the working directory and on other drives are accepted. **The result names the copy's absolute path**, so restoring a file never requires searching for it.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Protection before a change：**Destructive shell commands are refused once.** A `bash` / `pwsh` command that looks like it deletes files (`rm`, `del`, `rd`, `Remove-Item`, and so on) is denied, and the model is told to declare its targets through `worktree_backup` before retrying — a deletion cannot be recovered after it runs. Quoted spans do not count, so `echo "rm -rf /"` is not refused. The switch can be turned off in settings.

Rules worth knowing:

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Protection before a change：- **One copy per file.** A later change in the same session does not replace it, because the version worth keeping is the one from before the first change.
- **Only files that already exist.** A file the AI creates has no prior state. It *is* copied when a later session changes it — by then it exists.
- **One directory per session, deleted when the session is archived.** The archive's own durable write is the trigger, so the copies go as soon as it lands — a plain archive and a stop-and-archive behave the same. Failures log the session, directory, and reason and retry on later archive-related events; cancelling tools cannot recreate an archived session's backups. Only an archive that happens while the host runs is cleaned; earlier ones are never deleted retroactively.
- **No size cap.** One full set of copies is roughly the size of the workspace; measured on one machine, 243,529 files came to 12.72 GB.
- **Writes outside the working directory are not automatic**, so they rely on the AI declaring them through `worktree_backup`. A change the AI never declares is not copied — which is why destructive commands are refused un

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Protection before a change：For complete history, or recovery across machines and time, use Git commits. This feature exists for "the AI just broke this and I want the previous version back".

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Change history in the sidebar：**On by default.** The right sidebar offers a **Change history** page — open it from the sidebar's own Start page, and use the page-refresh shortcut inside it to read the list again. It lists the files **this session and its sub-sessions changed or deleted**, one flat row each and no directory tree, with only the path and a **Restore** button, without state badges. Deleted paths are struck through; a successful restore removes the strike. A row a sub-session took names that sub-session, so it cannot be confused with this session's file of the same path.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Change history in the sidebar：- **Modified** means the file's content no longer matches its copy; **Deleted** means the file is gone. A copy whose file is still byte-identical is left out, because there is nothing to restore.
- **Restore** writes that one copy back over its file, creating the directories again if the file had been deleted. The copy itself is kept, so the same row can put the file back after a later change.
- **Compare** — click a row's path to open a two-column view: the copy from before this session first changed the file on the left, the current file on the right, aligned line by line. Changed lines are tinted and sit opposite each other; a collapsed band stands for a run of unchanged lines. Each side scrolls sideways on its own because the two may have different line lengths, while vertical scrolling moves both together, and the view opens on the first change.
- The comparison compares **the two files on disk — no Git involved**, so it works the same whether or not Git is installed. Its left side is the state before this session's first change, so it shows everything changed since then, including edits another session made to a

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Git accounts and projects：The left sidebar gains a **Git accounts** page that puts this machine's Git identity in one place: sign in to GitHub, GitLab (including self-hosted addresses such as `gitlab.arcuchi.com`), and Gitee; set the global `user.name` and `user.email` used for commits; and browse your own projects.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Git accounts and projects：- **Sign-in method**: in **Add account**, pick the platform, confirm the server address, then choose an **access token** or an **SSH key** (no OAuth app registration); a separate **Test connection** button checks the credential without saving it. The Host verifies the credential against the platform and only then stores it — in the DSH credential store (`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`, readable only by the current user) — and a token is **never returned to the page or written to logs**. GitHub tokens need permission to list repositories (classic `repo`; fine-grained Metadata/Contents read), GitLab needs `read_api` (or `api`), and Gitee needs `projects` and `user_info`.
- **SSH-key sign-in**: pick a private key from this machine's `~/.ssh` (or type another path); the Host runs one non-interactive `ssh -T` so the platform can name the account that owns the key. **Only the key's path is stored — its contents are never read or uploaded**, host keys are recorded in a scratch file, and your existing `known_hosts` is left untouched. A connection test has a **five-second total budget**; GitHub and GitLab are retried over **port 443

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Git accounts and projects：> For a self-hosted GitLab with a self-signed certificate, the Host's Node runtime must trust that certificate; otherwise verification and project listing fail with a network error. Scanning reads credentials in the current user's context only — it never shows an OS authorization dialog or starts an interactive login.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Git accounts and projects：The connections are the first card on the **Settings → File backup** page, so an account can be added, scanned, or removed without opening the Git accounts panel first; the card's "View projects on the Git accounts page" control switches the main panel straight to the project list.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Install：```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add @guowenzhang/dsh-worktree
```

Restart DSH after installation. Git must be installed and available on the host's PATH.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Notes：- **Upgrading to 2.x**: model-facing Worktree tools have been removed. Create worktrees through the New Session control; archive notifications may clean up clean worktrees. Integrations that call the removed model tools must be updated.

@guowenzhang/dsh-worktree README · Notes：- **Multi-repository support is off by default**: enable “Create child repositories” in settings and adjust the scan depth to your directory layout (default: 1 level). Submodules use the commit recorded by the parent repository in detached HEAD; independent nested repositories get new branches.
- **Uncommitted changes are not copied**: the worktree starts from a commit on the selected branch, with an automatically generated branch name.
- **Storage defaults to inside the workspace**: `<workspace>/.agents/worktree/<branch>`. Add `.agents/worktree/` to your Git ignore rules, or choose a location beside the repository or in the user home directory.
- **New sessions can start in a worktree automatically**: with “Start new sessions in a worktree” on, the first blank session in a repository creates its own checkout and moves into it, without asking. Off by default.
